tools.name: set_clip_effects
tools.title: Set clip effects
tools.description: Set the effects a video clip wears over its own picture (negative, huecycle, grain, vhs, glitch, blur, vignette, lightleak, flash). They treat that clip alone — inside its mask, under its pose — for its whole length, on the clip's own clock: a masked copy over the shot wearing negative and huecycle shows a color-cycling negative window while the shot around it plays untouched. add_effect places an element that treats the whole frame under its window. Pass the full list in order; [] removes them all. amount 0.05..1 (default 0.5) is the strength; for huecycle it is how fast the hue turns (0.5 is a turn every 1.25s); negative has none, but takes a strobe rate: a cutout copy wearing negative at rate 15 flashes between negative and normal every frame. A flash takes add_effect's tone, rate, rhythm and fade on the clip's own clock: a white flicker at rate 12–15, amount 0.15–0.25, pops a masked shot's exposure unevenly while the black around the mask stays black. A subject flashed in over a shot — the next shot's subject cut out (set_removal) on a track above, landing as a solid white silhouette, then itself, then blown out, then itself — is that cutout split into a clip per frame of the flicker: fade "from" at amount 1 for the silhouette, a pop at 0.6-0.9 for each blown-out frame, nothing for the frames that show it plain. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

effects.description: The clip's effects, applied in this order

rate.description: flash and negative: strobe pulses a second, 0.5..15, each held for its first half (15 at 30 fps flips every other frame); omit for one pop at the clip's start, or a negative flipped throughout

rhythm.description: flash with a rate only: "strobe" (default) or "flicker", each pulse its own strength, some skipped

fade_ease.description: flash with a fade only: the curve it runs along, as add_effect takes it ("linear", the even ramp, by default)

fade.description: flash only: ramp evenly across the clip — "from" starts as the tone alone and clears, "to" ends on it. At amount 1 a one-frame clip fading from white is a solid silhouette of what it shows

tools.name: set_clip_hidden
tools.title: Set clip hidden
tools.description: Hide or show a video clip on any track. A hidden clip stays on the timeline (grayed) but is excluded from playback and export — its span plays black and silent on track 0; an overlay layer just disappears. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

tools.name: set_clip_keyframes
tools.title: Set clip keyframes
tools.description: Give a video clip (any track) a keyframed pose track: each key is a whole pose at a time measured in seconds from the clip's own start — center position in frame fractions, scale multiplier on its fitted size, rotation, opacity, blur — moving linearly between keys and holding outside them. Omitted fields on a key take the clip's pose at that moment. Pass an empty list to clear the track and return the clip to its region. Use for pans, push-ins, picture-in-picture flights, spins, and fades on video itself. blur softens the picture (px at the 1080 short side, 0..60); motion_blur streaks the picture along its keyed movement, so a panel that flies in with blur keyed from high to 0 and a shutter on lands as a smear that settles sharp. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

keys.description: Keys in any order; two at the same time collapse to one; omit to keep the track and change only the motion blur

x.description: Center x, fraction of frame width

y.description: Center y, fraction of frame height

scale.description: Size multiplier, 1 = the clip's fitted size (0.1..4)

rotation.description: Degrees clockwise, -180..180, to a tenth (0.4 matches a slight lean)

blur.description: Blur, px at the 1080 short side, 0..60

motion_blur.description: Streak the clip along its keyed movement while it moves (true starts at the default shutter); false switches it off; omitted keeps it

shutter.description: Motion blur shutter in 30fps frames, 0.05..4: 0.5 is the usual half-open shutter, and past 1 is a stylized long exposure (2–3 smears a whip that settles in a few frames); setting it switches motion blur on

tools.name: set_clip_muted
tools.title: Set clip muted
tools.description: Mute or unmute a video clip's own audio. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

tools.name: set_clip_sound
tools.title: Set clip sound
tools.description: Shape a clip's own sound — video clip or soundtrack clip — with the Sound quality section's three stages: a 7-band equalizer, a compressor, and a limiter. Each stage runs on that clip alone, before its fades and any ducking, in the preview and every export. Pass `preset` to apply a shipped treatment ("Flat", "Clear voice", "Warm & Rich", "Crisp & Clear", "Broadcast", "Natural", "Deep Voice", "Airy", "Studio", "Phone / Lo-Fi", "Cinematic", "Close / ASMR") or one the user saved, by name or id; or set the stages directly, leaving out the ones that stay as they are. `clear` names stages to remove, and the "Off" preset removes all three. Read the clip's current treatment from editor_state before a partial change. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

clipId.description: Video clip id or soundtrack clip id

preset.description: A preset by name or id, plus whatever the user has saved. Shipped: "Clear voice" (clear-voice) — Warm, clear podcast voice; "Warm & Rich" (warm-rich) — Deep, smooth, expensive-sounding; "Crisp & Clear" (crisp-clear) — Bright, clean, highly intelligible; "Broadcast" (broadcast) — Polished podcast/radio voice, more compressed; "Natural" (natural) — Balanced, close to the real voice; "Deep Voice" (deep-voice) — Darker, heavier, deeper without turning muddy; "Airy" (airy) — Bright, open, modern creator voice; "Studio" (studio) — Warm, clear, controlled, professional — the talking-head default; "Phone / Lo-Fi" (phone) — Narrow, mid-heavy, phone-like; for skits, flashbacks and transitions; "Cinematic" (cinematic) — Warm, dark, intimate storytelling voice; "Close / ASMR" (close-asmr) — Intimate, close, detailed. "Off" (flat) leaves the clip's sound as it came.

clear.description: Stages to remove from the clip's treatment.

eq.description: Gain in dB per band, −12..+12, in this order: 100 Hz, 200 Hz, 400 Hz, 1 kHz, 3 kHz, 5 kHz, 10 kHz (the first band is a low shelf, the last a high shelf, the rest peaks). Fewer values leave the remaining bands flat.

tools.name: set_clip_style
tools.title: Set clip style
tools.description: Style a video clip's box: rounded corners, a border ring along its edge, and a drop shadow cast by the clip's shape (its box, corners, and mask together — a circle-masked clip casts a circular shadow). Lengths are design px at the 1080 short side. Only the fields you pass change; pass clear:true to remove all styling. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

radius.description: Corner radius, design px (0 squares the corners)

border_width.description: Border stroke width, design px (0 removes the ring)

shadow_blur.description: Shadow blur radius, design px; 0 with no offset removes the shadow

tools.name: set_clip_volume
tools.title: Set clip volume
tools.description: Set the gain on a video clip's own audio (soundtrack clips use update_audio). It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

volume.description: 0..3 (1 = unchanged, up to 3 boosts the clip's own sound)

tools.name: set_color_curves
tools.title: Set color curves
tools.description: Set a video clip's tone curves: per-channel [input, output] control points (0..255) through a monotone spline — master shapes all three channels, red/green/blue shape one each. A channel you pass replaces that channel; an empty list clears it; others keep their curve. curve_contrast (-50..50) writes an s-curve around mid-gray into the master curve for you, replacing it (lifted, faded blacks are the fade slider of set_color_grade). reset:true clears every curve first. Pass ids or all_clips to land the same curves on several clips. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

all_clips.description: Land the change on every clip on the timeline (instead of clipId or ids)

master.description: Master curve control points as [input, output] pairs (0..255, sorted by input); replaces that channel; an empty list clears it

red.description: Red curve control points as [input, output] pairs (0..255, sorted by input); replaces that channel; an empty list clears it

green.description: Green curve control points as [input, output] pairs (0..255, sorted by input); replaces that channel; an empty list clears it

blue.description: Blue curve control points as [input, output] pairs (0..255, sorted by input); replaces that channel; an empty list clears it

tools.name: set_color_grade
tools.title: Set color grade
tools.description: Color-grade a video clip's basic sliders (any track; stills too): the Light group (exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, brilliance, fade), the Color group (temperature, tint, saturation, vibrance) and the Detail pair (sharpen, clarity). Fields patch the clip's current grade: only the ones you pass change, and every value 0 is neutral. The light sliders work in linear light: on the picture after its source conversion and LUT, and on log footage on the camera's scene light, ahead of the ACES output transform and the LUT. The manual grade balances the shot first and the clip's color preset (set_color_preset) styles the corrected picture on top; both stay. reset:true clears the manual grade first (the preset and LUT stay); auto:true fits a starting grade from the clip's base rendering (auto-tone: exposure to middle gray, contrast stretch, gray-world white balance), and explicit fields then override it. Preview, timeline thumbnails, and export all render the same result. Read read_color_stats before grading so the numbers ground the move. Pass ids or all_clips to land the same patch on several clips as one undo step. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

all_clips.description: Land the change on every clip on the timeline (instead of clipId or ids)

highlights.description: -50..50, 0 neutral — trim (-) or boost (+) the brights

shadows.description: -50..50, 0 neutral — lift (+) or crush (-) the darks

whites.description: -50..50, 0 neutral — the white point: pull (-) or push (+) the very brightest values

blacks.description: -50..50, 0 neutral — the black point: lift (+) or deepen (-) the very darkest values

brilliance.description: -50..50, 0 neutral — brings up the darks and tames the brights together, like a photo app's brilliance

fade.description: 0..50, 0 neutral — lifts the blacks toward grey for a faded-film look

temperature.description: -50..50, 0 neutral — positive = warmer (mireds, CAT02 white balance)

vibrance.description: -50..50, 0 neutral — saturation weighted toward the muted colors

clarity.description: 0..50, 0 neutral — local contrast across larger structures (luma only)

hue.description: Whole-frame hue rotation in degrees, -180..180 (for one hue only, use set_color_hsl)

auto.description: Fit a starting grade from the clip's current frame

reset.description: Clear the existing manual grade before applying fields (keeps the preset and the LUT)

tools.name: set_color_hsl
tools.title: Set color hsl
tools.description: Adjust one hue band of a video clip — shift its hue (±50 ≈ ±30°), scale its saturation, and lift or darken its luminance — leaving every other color alone ("just the sky bluer", "mute the greens"). Bands: red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, purple, magenta. The band's three values are replaced whole (omitted values 0); all-zero clears the band. reset_all clears every band first. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

all_clips.description: Land the change on every clip on the timeline (instead of clipId or ids)

tools.name: set_color_lut
tools.title: Set color lut
tools.description: Put a LUT on a video clip, or take it off. editor_state.luts lists every LUT by id ("lut:<key>"): the built-in film looks, marked builtIn — Portrait (warm, glowing skin, a touch brighter; flattering on people); Natural (gently warm, true-to-life color, clean whites); Airy (bright and light, lifted midtones, warm with a little more color); Vivid (saturated, warm slide-film color with strong contrast); Heritage (rich reds, restrained greens, crisp whites; classic slide film); Crisp (neutral color, deeper midtones, clean whites); Pop (saturated and dense, deep reds, darker midtones); Street (warm, punchy everyday film color, bright whites); Summer (hot reds and magentas, saturated, darker midtones); Cross Process (strong cyan-blue cast, saturated; surreal); Snapshot (faded instant film: lifted blacks, muted, cool-green shadows); Warm Fade (warm, lifted blacks, bright highlights; sunny faded film); Nostalgic (muted and softly faded, slightly cooler; old prints); Dusty (dark, dense amber-brown, muted greens); Press (black and white, even tones, bright whites); Documentary (black and white, dark and contrasty); Infrared (black and white, very bright, glowing highlights and foliage); Retro Mono (black and white, hard contrast, deep blacks) — and the user's own .cube/.3dl files in the Library. The LUT is applied to the picture after the clip's source conversion and under the grade, so a creative LUT works on log footage and the sliders shape what comes out. amount 0..1 mixes the LUT's result with its input (default 1). Pass lut "none" to remove it. A Log-to-Rec.709 technical LUT (a camera maker's) belongs on a clip whose source color is set to rec709 (set_source_color) so it is not converted twice. Pass ids or all_clips to land the same LUT on several clips as one undo step. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

all_clips.description: Land the change on every clip on the timeline (instead of clipId or ids)

lut.description: A LUT id ("lut:<key>", from editor_state.luts) or "none" to remove the LUT

amount.description: Intensity 0..1 (default 1; omitted keeps the clip's current amount)

tools.name: set_color_preset
tools.title: Set color preset
tools.description: Apply a named color preset to a video clip, layered over its manual grade. Presets by category — Cinematic: teal-orange (Teal & Orange: warm skin over teal shadows, extra saturation; blockbuster), bleach-bypass (Bleach Bypass: desaturated and silvery, crushed blacks; gritty), matinee (Matinee: very warm, rich saturated color; classic Hollywood), thriller (Thriller: cool and muted, darker, crushed blacks; tense), night-market (Night Market: warm and saturated, slightly dim; night streets), sci-fi (Sci-Fi: cooler and slightly muted, clean blacks; slide film), push-process (Push Process: high contrast, dark midtones, bright whites; pushed film), cine-print (Cine Print: dark, dense print contrast, warm), tungsten (Tungsten: warm and saturated, softly lifted blacks), instant (Instant: bright, washed-out instant photo, lifted blacks), expired (Expired: faded and color-shifted, lifted blacks, muted); Warm: golden-hour (Golden Hour: warm, saturated sunset glow), amber (Amber: strong amber cast, lifted blacks), honey (Honey: soft warm yellow, gentle), sunbaked (Sunbaked: warm, a little more saturated, deep blacks), peach (Peach: warm pink-orange, softly lifted blacks), sepia (Sepia: brown-toned, near monochrome), ember (Ember: intense red-orange, deep blacks), bronze (Bronze: warm and metallic, muted, bright whites); Mood: midnight (Midnight: cool, dark and muted; night), moss (Moss: olive green, muted, earthy), slate (Slate: cool grey, desaturated), dusk (Dusk: warm magenta-red, dimmed highlights), neon (Neon: saturated magenta-red, deep blacks; nightlife), arctic (Arctic: cold blue-cyan, muted), storm (Storm: dark, muted and cool; overcast), velvet (Velvet: deep warm red, dark and rich); B&W: mono (Mono: neutral black and white), silver (Silver: soft, silvery black and white, lifted blacks), ink (Ink: hard-contrast black and white, deep blacks), high-key (High Key: bright, airy black and white), low-key (Low Key: dark, moody black and white), charcoal (Charcoal: flat grey black and white), soft-mono (Soft Mono: soft, low-contrast black and white), grit (Grit: gritty, high-contrast black and white). amount 0..1 scales the preset toward neutral (default 1); protect_skin keeps its color shifts off skin tones. Pass preset "none" to clear. Preview, tiles, and export all render the same result. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

all_clips.description: Land the change on every clip on the timeline (instead of clipId or ids)

tools.name: set_color_wheels
tools.title: Set color wheels
tools.description: Set a video clip's four color wheels — lift, gamma, gain, offset — the ASC CDL set: lift moves the shadows, gamma the midtones, gain the highlights, and offset shifts the whole picture equally. Each wheel pushes its range toward a hue (dx/dy is the wheel puck: angle = hue, 0° = red, 120° = green, 240° = blue; distance = strength) and trims its brightness (luma). A wheel you pass is replaced whole; {dx:0,dy:0,luma:0} clears it. reset:true clears all four. Pass ids or all_clips to land the same wheels on several clips. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

tools.name: set_framing
tools.title: Set framing
tools.description: Set how a video clip meets its box (the project frame, or its region): 'fit' letterboxes the whole picture (default), 'fill' scales it to cover the box and crops the overflow. zoom pushes further in from there, 1..4. Whenever the picture overflows, panX/panY (-1..1, 0=centered) choose what stays visible — e.g. panY=-1 keeps the top. flipH mirrors the picture left for right (a front-camera take that reads backward, text and all, wants flipH true), flipV top for bottom. Only the fields you pass change; the rest of the clip's framing stays. Landscape footage in a vertical project usually wants fill plus a pan that holds the subject. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

panX.description: Crop pan -1 (left) .. 1 (right), when the picture overflows

panY.description: Crop pan -1 (top) .. 1 (bottom), when the picture overflows

tools.name: set_group_camera
tools.title: Set group camera
tools.description: Give a group of elements (titles, shapes, stickers) one camera that moves over them as a single world: steps from card to card, pushes onto the one being talked about, pulls back, whips. Each key is a camera pose at a time in seconds from the group's start (its earliest element): x/y is the world point at the frame's center (frame fractions, where the elements' own x/y live), scale is the zoom (1 = as laid out, 2.5 = a card a few tenths of the frame wide fills it; 0.25..8), rotation turns the whole world clockwise about the frame center. ease is the curve out of a key into the next (linear, sine.in, sine.out, sine.inOut, power2.in, power2.out, power2.inOut, power3.in, power3.out, power3.inOut; default linear): sine.inOut glides between cards, power3.out lands a push, power3.inOut over a short gap is a whip. Every element keeps its own keyframes and animation, composed inside the camera. To focus a card, push onto it and blur and dim its neighbours with set_overlay_keyframes keys (blur, opacity) at the same moments. motion_blur streaks what the camera's movement does (shutter sets how hard); an element's own motion_blur (update_overlay) streaks its whole on-screen movement instead. Name the group by group_id or by any member ids. Omitted fields on a key take the camera's pose at that moment; keys replace the whole track; an empty list clears the camera. Group the cards first (group_items), lay them out across and beyond the frame — a grouped element's x/y reaches -1..2 — then key the camera. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

group_id.description: Group id (from editor_state groupCameras or an element's groupId)

ids.description: Member ids, in place of group_id: their group takes the camera

keys.description: Camera keys in any order; two at the same time collapse to one

x.description: World point at the frame center, fraction of frame width, -1..2

y.description: World point at the frame center, fraction of frame height, -1..2

motion_blur.description: Streak the camera's moves (true starts at the default shutter); false switches it off

shutter.description: Motion blur shutter in 30fps frames, 0.05..4: 0.5 is the usual half-open shutter, and past 1 is a stylized long exposure (2–3 smears a whip that settles in a few frames); setting it switches motion blur on

tools.name: set_guides
tools.title: Set guides
tools.description: Choose the guides drawn over the preview — lines and shaded keep-out regions that show where titles, stickers and captions can sit. They draw in the editor only and never export. Presets: thirds (Thirds), center (Center), margins (Safe margins, 5% inset), shortform (Short form, tiktok, instagram, youtube), custom (Custom, drag lines on the preview). The short-form preset shades the phone UI of TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts merged — top bar, right-hand action rail, bottom caption block, and the side strips Reels and Shorts crop when they fill a taller phone screen — and fits portrait frames. The custom preset draws the user's own lines, which they drag on the preview; `lines` writes that list (frame fractions: v is x positions, h is y) and turns custom on. `show` replaces the whole set; [] turns every guide off. Placement never needs a guide on: editor_state project.safeZones already carries every preset's safe area for the frame. project.guides reports what shows and the custom lines. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

show.description: Guide ids to show; replaces the current set

lines.description: Custom lines to draw, replacing the current ones: v = vertical line x positions, h = horizontal line y positions, each 0..1 of the frame

tools.name: set_magnet
tools.title: Set magnet
tools.description: Turn the project's magnet on or off. On, track 0 stays closed up: deleting, trimming or moving a clip there pulls everything after it left, and the clips on other tracks, the elements, captions and soundtrack move with the track-0 footage under their start, keeping their lengths (one over a closed gap lands on the join). Nothing can land below track 0 while it is on. Off, track 0 keeps its gaps, which play the background. Turning it on closes every gap at once. It is the user's setting: call it when they ask for the magnet, ripple editing, or a track 0 that never has gaps; remove_gap closes one gap. editor_state project.magnet reports it. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

on.description: true turns the magnet on, false turns it off

tools.name: set_mask
tools.title: Set mask
tools.description: Mask an overlay element or a video clip — trim its picture to a shape or to the person in the shot. Kinds: rect (rounded box), square (rounded square, side = w of the frame width), circle (ellipse; w and h are frame fractions, so a perfect circle needs w × frame width = h × frame height — omitting h gives you that circle), linear (half-plane: at rotation 0 the top side stays), mirror (band across the item), heart / star / triangle / diamond / hexagon (the outline filled into the w × h box, point up), pen (an outline you give as `points` — the shape for any region the fixed shapes miss: the gap between two hands, a doorway, a screen in the shot; its box defaults to the whole frame, w = h = 1, so a point is an offset from the item's center in frame fractions, (-0.5, -0.5) the frame's top-left corner; the box's position, size, rotation and keys then carry the whole drawing), subject (the person matte: invert true sits the item behind the speaker; invert false keeps it only on the person — an element newly masked as subject defaults to behind, a clip to on-person). Position is the mask center's offset from the item's own center (a clip's region center), in frame fractions; w/h size it in frame fractions; feather softens the edge; invert keeps what the shape leaves out; radius rounds a rect or square's corners. Subject masks use only feather and invert. Pass kind "none" to remove the mask. `keys` animates the geometry over time — each key is the full geometry at a moment, moving linearly between keys; pass an empty list to clear the keys and keep the mask still. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

id.description: Overlay element id or video clip id

kind.description: Mask shape, the person matte ("subject"), or "none" to remove the mask

x.description: Center offset x from the element center, fraction of frame width (default 0)

y.description: Center offset y, fraction of frame height (default 0)

w.description: Width, fraction of frame width (default 0.5; square: the side; linear ignores)

h.description: Height, fraction of frame height (mirror: band height; square/linear ignore)

rotation.description: Degrees clockwise, -180..180, to a tenth (0.4 matches a slight lean)

feather.description: Edge softness, px at the 1080 design short side (0..600)

invert.description: Keep the pixels outside the shape

radius.description: Rect or square corner radius, px at 1080 short side (0..400)

points.description: Pen only: the outline's corners in order around it, at least 3, each an offset from the mask center in fractions of the mask box (with the pen's default w = h = 1: frame fractions from the item's center, -0.5..0.5 inside the frame); replaces the outline

x.description: Offset x, fraction of the mask box width

y.description: Offset y, fraction of the mask box height

keys.description: Mask keyframes, seconds from the element's start; omitted fields on a key take the mask's value at that moment

x.description: Center offset x, fraction of frame width

y.description: Center offset y, fraction of frame height

rotation.description: Degrees clockwise, -180..180, to a tenth (0.4 matches a slight lean)

feather.description: Edge softness, px at 1080 short side

radius.description: Rect or square corner radius, px at 1080 short side

tools.name: set_overlay_animation
tools.title: Set overlay animation
tools.description: Animate an overlay element (title, shape, or sticker): preset In/Out ramps, a Loop that runs its whole duration, and a Move that says what the element does WHILE it holds. Omitted slots keep their setting; pass "none" to clear one. In/Out styles: fade, pop, zoom, slideleft, slideright, slideup, slidedown, typewriter, wipe, rise, drop, grow, flip, swivel, bounce, wave, converge, streak, tumble, scatter, slot, dive, count, disintegrate, blur, glitch, flicker — slide names are the motion direction; typewriter, slot, count animate titles only; rise, drop, grow, flip, swivel, bounce, wave, converge, streak, tumble, scatter, slot, blur, glitch, flicker move a title's letters one at a time, and move any other kind as one piece; in_stagger/out_stagger set how much of their ramp the hand-off from the first letter to the last takes, so a 1.6s drop at stagger 0.8 lands a letter every ~0.27s, each moving for ~0.3s. in_order/out_order "shuffle" deals the letters their turns in a scattered order instead of left to right — letters landing at random; in_sequence names the exact order when it is read off a reference. in_ease sets the curve the move travels on, in_fade false keeps letters solid while they fall, and in_blur starts each letter out of focus (design px) to sharpen as it lands. in_distance/out_distance set how far the motion travels from rest, design px. A slot entrance's reel takes its shape off the reference too: in_reel (the way it turns), in_reel_pitch (how far apart its characters sit), in_reel_band (how far it shows above and below the line), in_overshoot and in_settle (a landing that runs past its slot and settles back), and in_fade false keeps every character on it solid. A reference's letters coming in are read in one call, never by eye: track_element match letters with the line's words over the stretch they come in returns `entrance`, every one of these settings as it goes in (in_style, in_seconds, in_stagger, in_sequence, in_sequence_at — each letter's own turn — in_distance, in_ease, in_fade — false, a share of the move, or true — and in_blur; for a slot reel its in_reel settings, for letters typed in place a typewriter's in_seconds) and the source second the ramp starts — one letter's move is in_seconds × (1 − in_stagger). A per-letter ramp on an element with update_overlay motion_blur streaks each letter along its own move, the smear a fast fall wears — a different look from a soft start. slot: Each letter rolls up through other characters like a slot reel and lands in turn. dive: The camera flies into the last letter until its ink fills the frame. On In it pulls back out of the letter. count: Every number in a title counts up from zero to its written value, one step at a time: a loading percentage, a stat, a price. Decimals and leading zeros keep their written form; on Out the numbers count back down to zero. disintegrate: The element crumbles away in grain: blotches of its ink are eaten until nothing is left, the gritty exit of a teaser title; on In it assembles out of the grain. blur: Letters sharpen out of a soft blur one at a time, in a shuffled order, each drifting into its line: the dreamy title reveal. On Out they melt back into the blur. glitch: Letters snap in one after another, torn into red and cyan copies that jitter sideways and lock together: the digital glitch title. On Out they tear apart and drop out. flicker: Letters blink on and off at random, each on its own beat, a few out at any moment, until the line locks on: the failing-neon title. On Out the line breaks into the same flicker within a few frames and keeps failing to the end. dive as the exit is the zoom-through-a-letter transition: the shot after the element shows once the ink has filled the frame, so it needs no freeze frames, image stills or per-letter keyframes. It flies the last letter's deepest ink to the frame's centre; a reference that zooms about a fixed point instead — the letter grows where it stands, its ink spreading out from one spot — takes out_anchor, the point track_camera reads over the zoom. On a dive out_ease is the flight's pace on its own clock — power2.in holds back and rushes into the ink at the end — and the ink fills the frame as the exit ends, so end it where the reference's frame fills. Loop styles: pulse, heartbeat, float, sway, spin, wiggle, shake, flicker, wave, bounce, flip, flutter — wave, bounce, flip, flutter carry a title's letters on their own delays, and carry any other kind as one piece. A move is a slot like the others and never touches the element's keyframe track; set_overlay_keyframes is the precise way to move an element and the default reach, so name a move when it is exactly what you mean — the two compose together. Word effects — words_style, titles only — play the line word by word, timed against the cut's transcript when there is one and spread across the element's own span when there is not: an emphasis travels along a line that is fully up, and a build assembles the line as it is spoken. It is the slot for "make each word pop as I say it" and for "have the words appear one by one". A typewriter entrance on a title can carry a caret: a thin bar at the end of the typed text, solid while it types, then blinking every 0.53s — the typed comment or search box of a call-to-action card. A hit plays one motion once at a moment inside the element (hit_at seconds from its start), between its entrance and exit: press: a finger tapping a button: the element dips to 93% and springs back, and darkens while it is held down when darken is on zap: electric arcs crackle over the element: blue-white bolts with a flare where each lands, re-dealt a dozen times a second, sparking up fast and dying out at the end — the charged beat of a teaser title. Use press for a button being pressed, a tap on a UI element, a like or post button; pair it with a click from stock_search kind "sound" placed at the same moment when the tap should be heard. A font cycle flickers a title through typefaces — a new face font_cycle_rate times a second, from font_cycle_at for font_cycle_seconds — and then the title settles back into its own face: the typeface-shuffle beat of a teaser title. Give each face a scale (and tracking) so it fills about the room the title's own face does; a wide tracked title cycling through condensed or hand-drawn faces wants tracking 0 and a scale above 1 on them. A face keeps the title's own line breaks: where its scale makes a line wider than the room the title wraps in, that face is set smaller to fit rather than broken onto another line. Time the faces to the music with font_cycle_beats — a new face on each beat of that clip's detect_beats grid, font_cycle_beat_step 2 for every other beat or 0.5 for half beats — or to a reference's own face changes with font_cycle_switches, the timeline seconds you read them at; either sets every hold and repeats the faces in order to fill the run. A face's own hold times one face by hand; faces repeat in the list to revisit a typeface. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

move.description: What the element does while it holds. push: A slow zoom in across the whole hold — the workhorse for a line that has to feel urgent. pull: A slow zoom out, the frame opening up. Endings, reveals, the last line of a verse. settle: Lands oversized and leaning, eases to rest in the first third, then creeps. Hero lines. swing: Overshoots past its resting angle and swings back. Playful, hand-drawn. punch: Snaps big, snaps back, then creeps. A hit on the beat. float: Rises a little the whole time it is up. Dreamy, weightless. sink: Drifts down. Regret, endings, a line that gives up. driftleft: Slides steadily left across the hold — a parallax bed under other lines. driftright: Slides steadily right. sway: Leans one way, then the other, and back to level. Drunk, loose, swung. arc: Travels along a shallow curve rather than a straight line. tiltsettle: Arrives rotated a quarter turn out and unwinds to level. breathe: Grows and shrinks a few percent, twice. Living, patient. creep: A scale rise so slow you only notice it in the cut. Dread, tension. slam: Enormous for two frames, then hard down to rest. Impact. orbit: Circles its own resting point once. Playful chaos. spring: Overshoots the size and bounces once past it before resting. fall: Drops in from above resting position and stops dead. Weight. reveal: Starts offset up at zero opacity and eases down into place.

move_strength.description: How hard the move pushes, 0.25..2 (1 = as written). Scales every offset from rest and leaves the timing alone, so the move stays on the beat.

in_seconds.description: Entrance ramp seconds 0.1..2 (default 0.5; typewriter up to 10; count up to 10; the per-letter styles up to 4)

out_seconds.description: Exit ramp seconds 0.1..2 (default 0.5; typewriter up to 10; count up to 10; the per-letter styles up to 4)

in_stagger.description: Per-letter entrance: share of the ramp spent handing the motion from the first letter to the last, 0..0.95 (0 = every letter together, higher = one after another, each moving for less of the ramp); a negative restores the style's own

out_stagger.description: Per-letter exit: the same hand-off share for the exit ramp, 0..0.95; a negative restores the style's own

in_order.description: Per-letter entrance: the order the letters take their turns — "reading" (left to right) or "shuffle" (a fixed scattered order)

out_order.description: Per-letter exit: the same order for the exit ramp

in_sequence.description: Per-letter entrance in an order read off a reference: the letters' numbers in the order they arrive, counting the title's letters from 0 and skipping spaces (YOUR LOCATION: Y=0 … R=3, L=4 … N=11). Overrides in_order; [] clears it

out_sequence.description: Per-letter exit: the letters' numbers in the order they leave; [] clears it

in_sequence_at.description: With in_sequence: when each of its letters starts, in its order, as a share of the hand-off — 0 the first, 1 the last — for a reference whose letters do not go evenly spaced (track_element match letters reads it). [] spaces them evenly

out_sequence_at.description: With out_sequence: each letter's turn as a share of the hand-off; [] spaces them evenly

in_ease.description: Entrance: the curve the move travels on — the ease track_element reads for the reference's move (linear for a steady fall, an .out ease for one that brakes into place); "style" restores the style's own

out_ease.description: Exit: the same curve for the exit ramp; "style" restores the style's own

in_fade.description: Entrance: false keeps the element (each letter) solid the whole way in instead of fading up as it moves — a letter falling in from beyond the frame is solid; a share of the move, 0..1, fades it up over that much and holds it solid after; true restores the style's fade

out_fade.description: Exit: false keeps it solid the whole way out; a share of the move fades it over that much; true restores the style's fade

in_blur.description: Entrance: how soft each letter (the element) starts, design px of defocus, 0..60, sharpening on the move's curve as it lands; 0 keeps a soft style sharp, -1 restores the style's own

out_blur.description: Exit: how soft it ends, design px; 0 keeps it sharp, -1 restores the style's own

in_distance.description: Entrance: how far the motion travels from rest at its far end, design px at 1080, 1..4000; 0 restores the style's own reach

out_distance.description: Exit: the same reach for the exit ramp, design px; 0 restores the style's own

in_reel.description: Slot entrance: which way the reel turns — "up" brings each character in from below, "down" from above (a landing letter that arrives from above, whatever a fast spin seems to do between frames); "style" restores the style's own (up). track_element match letters reads it

in_reel_pitch.description: Slot entrance: how far apart the reel's characters sit, design px at 1080 (kept in em of the title's size, up to 4 em); 0 restores the style's own, tighter than a line

in_reel_band.description: Slot entrance: how far the band the reel shows through reaches above and below the line's middle, design px; 0 restores the style's own (the line itself)

in_overshoot.description: Slot entrance: how far, design px, each character's reel runs past its slot before it settles back — a landing bounce; 0 clears it

in_settle.description: Slot entrance with an overshoot: the share of each character's move spent settling back, 0.05..0.6 (default 0.3)

x.description: Frame x, 0..1

y.description: Frame y, 0..1

in_anchor.description: Dive entrance: the frame point the zoom holds still as it pulls back out, frame fractions — track_camera's anchor; "none" restores the deepest ink flying from the frame's centre

x.description: Frame x, 0..1

y.description: Frame y, 0..1

out_anchor.description: Dive exit: the frame point the zoom holds still as it flies in, frame fractions — track_camera's anchor over the reference's zoom; "none" restores the deepest ink of the last letter flying to the frame's centre

loop_speed.description: Loop rate multiplier 0.25..8 (default 1); one cycle takes its base time over the speed — pulse 1.2s, heartbeat 1.5s, float 2.4s, sway 2.8s, spin 4s, wiggle 0.9s, shake 0.5s, flicker 1.8s, wave 1.6s, bounce 1.6s, flip 3.2s, flutter 1.4s — so a loading spinner that turns once every 0.8s is spin at speed 5

words_style.description:
What each word does as it is said, or "none" to clear.
Emphasis — the treatment travels along the line, one word at a time: color (the word being said takes the accent color and hands it on); pop (the word swells and the line makes room for it, in the text's own color unless an accent is set); underline (accent color with a rule under the word); box (an accent box behind the word); spotlight (the line sits faded and only the word being said is at full strength)
Build — the line assembles itself as it is spoken: build (the line starts empty and each word appears as it is said, completing the sentence); fill (the whole line is up but faint, and each word goes solid as it is said until the sentence is fully opaque); rise (each word lifts into its place as it is said and stays); bloom (each word grows out of nothing into its size as it is said and stays); swing (each word drops in leaning and rights itself as it is said); paint (the line is written in its own color and each word takes the accent as it is said, keeping it)

words_scale.description: How far a word swells at its moment, 1..2 (pop defaults to 1.24, the effects that do not resize stay at 1). The swollen word takes its new width in the line, so its neighbours move aside and settle back as the emphasis travels on.

words_dim.description: How opaque a word is off its moment, 0..1 — 0 means it is not there yet (build), a fraction leaves the line faintly visible (fill, spotlight). Effects that do not fade their words ignore it.

caret.description: Typewriter entrance only: show a typing caret at the end of the typed text (false removes it)

caret_blink.description: Whether the caret blinks once typing stops (default true); false holds it solid

caret_blinks.description: How many times the caret blinks before it stops, 1..20; 0 blinks for as long as the element is up (default)

caret_hide.description: Remove the caret after its last blink (or right after typing when it does not blink)

caret_color.description: Caret color (hex); default is the text color

hit_style.description: One-shot hit played once inside the element, or "none" to clear

hit_at.description: Seconds from the element's start where the hit begins

hit_darken.description: Darken the element while the hit holds it down (default true for a new hit)

font_cycle.description: Titles only: the faces the title cycles through, in order (up to 48); [] removes the cycle

weight.description: Weight of this face; default the title's own

scale.description: Size multiplier on the title's own size, 0.5..4 (default 1)

tracking.description: Letter spacing in em for this face; default the title's own

italic.description: Italic for this face; default the title's own

hold.description: Seconds this face shows, up to 10; default one step at font_cycle_rate

font_cycle_at.description: Seconds from the element's start where the cycle begins (default 0)

font_cycle_seconds.description: How long the cycle runs, seconds (default: to the element's end)

font_cycle_rate.description: Face changes a second, 2..30 (default 15: a new face every other frame at 30 fps)

font_cycle_switches.description: Timeline seconds where the face changes, in order: the first shows the first face, each next one the next face, and the last returns the title to its own face (the title's end keeps the last face up). Sets every face's hold

font_cycle_beats.description: Clip id (soundtrack or video) whose beat grid times the faces: a new face on each beat inside the run, the last held to the run's end. Call detect_beats on that clip first

font_cycle_beat_step.description: Beats per face with font_cycle_beats: 1 (default), 2 every other beat, 0.5 two faces a beat

tools.name: set_overlay_keyframes
tools.title: Set overlay keyframes
tools.description: Give an overlay element a keyframed pose track — the default way to animate one, because a key names the exact pose at the exact second where a preset ramp approximates it. Each key is a whole pose at a time measured in seconds from the element's own start; the pose moves between keys along the key's ease (linear, sine.in, sine.out, sine.inOut, power2.in, power2.out, power2.inOut, power3.in, power3.out, power3.inOut; default linear) and holds outside them. Omitted fields on a key take the element's current value. scale_x/scale_y stretch one side over scale (a screen switching off: scale_y to 0.02, then scale_x to 0.02); tilt_x/tilt_y turn the element in 3D perspective about its horizontal/vertical axis (tilt_x positive tips the top edge away, tilt_y the right edge; ±85°): a bar falling back, a card swinging open. blur softens the element (px at the 1080 short side, 0..60): keyed with opacity it is depth of field — the card being read sharp, its neighbours blurred and dimmed while a group camera (set_group_camera) pushes in. Keys merge into the track the element already has — one at an existing time replaces that key, the rest stay — so pass replace true to lay a new track over an old one in one call. Pass an empty list to clear the track and return the element to its resting pose. Preset In/Out/Loop animation still composes on top, so a keyframed title can also fade in. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

replace.description: true drops the element's existing keys first; default false merges these into them

keys.description: Keys in any order; two at the same time collapse to one

x.description: Center x, fraction of frame width, -0.5..1.5: past 0..1 the element sits beyond the edge, for one that enters or leaves across it, like a pointer sliding in from below (-1..2 for a grouped element)

y.description: Center y, fraction of frame height, -0.5..1.5 (-1..2 for a grouped element)

scale.description: Size multiplier, 1 = the element's own size (0.1..4)

rotation.description: Degrees clockwise, -180..180, to a tenth (0.4 matches a slight lean)

tilt_x.description: 3D tilt about the horizontal axis, degrees, -85..85; positive tips the top edge away (default 0)

tilt_y.description: 3D tilt about the vertical axis, degrees, -85..85; positive tips the right edge away (default 0)

blur.description: Blur, px at the 1080 short side, 0..60

tools.name: set_project_color
tools.title: Set project color
tools.description: Set the project's delivery color space: sdr = SDR (Rec.709, BT.1886, 100 nits.); hlg = HDR (HLG) (Rec.2100 HLG, 1000-nit reference display.); pq = HDR (PQ) (Rec.2100 PQ, 1000-nit reference display.). The export writes it — an HDR project encodes 10-bit HEVC Main 10 or ProRes tagged Rec.2020 with the HLG or PQ transfer, and H.264 is not offered — and the preview shows the HDR picture on an HDR display, or the same grade rendered as SDR with a "Previewing SDR" label elsewhere. SDR footage placed in an HDR project sits at reference white (BT.2408); HLG and PQ footage keeps its range. Call it when the user asks for HDR, HLG, PQ, Rec.2100, or to go back to SDR; editor_state project.colorSpace reports the current one. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

tools.name: set_project_name
tools.title: Set project name
tools.description: Rename the current project. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

tools.name: set_project_notes
tools.title: Set project notes
tools.description: Write this project's own notes — the Details tab's date, links and text, saved with the project for anyone who opens it. Put a cut's sources here: the original video a template copies, the post it was published as, a reference. note_save writes the account's synced notes, kept in the Library, which travel with no project. add_links appends (skipping links already there); links replaces the whole list. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

add_links.description: Links to append, kept in order, duplicates skipped

links.description: The whole link list, replacing what is there ([] clears it)

text.description: Free text, replacing what is there

tools.name: set_publish
tools.title: Set publish
tools.description: Set the TikTok publish metadata: caption (4,000 char limit incl. tags), tags (space-separated words, # added automatically), soundTitle, handle. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

tools.name: set_removal
tools.title: Set removal
tools.description: Cut out a subject or background on any video track. mode auto starts the free person matte; custom tracks the subject described in subject and spends credits; off keeps the stored matte and settings. remove background keeps the subject, and remove subject keeps its surroundings. refine requests the paid quality upgrade when the user asks for it. Matting continues in the editor: inspect_project reports each clip's removal readiness and progress. Check readiness before claiming completion, then capture_frame to inspect the result. The user can select an exact instance with the Cutout inspector's brush and Apply controls. Read background-removal for the workflow. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

remove.description: What goes: "background" (default) keeps the selection, "subject" removes it and keeps the rest of the picture

refine.description: Auto mode: also run the hosted quality pass for hair and edge detail once the free matte lands — spends credits like generation, so pass it only when the user asks for the upgrade (the panel's "Apply")

subject.description: Custom mode: what to keep, in a few words ("the dog", "the red car") — every match is matted and tracked

tools.name: set_removal_background
tools.title: Set removal background
tools.description: Fill in behind a cutout clip's subject (the clip needs an active set_removal cutout): a flat color or a project image asset drawn where the removed background was, inside the clip's own picture. Kind "none" clears the fill and lets lower tracks show through again. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

asset_id.description: Project image asset id (kind "image")

tools.name: set_removal_stroke
tools.title: Set removal stroke
tools.description: Draw ink around a cutout clip's silhouette (the clip needs an active set_removal cutout). Styles: glow (glow), hand (hand drawn), cut (straight cut), solid (solid), offset (offset), dotted (dotted) — glow haloes the edge, hand looks marker-drawn, cut is a coarse straight-edged sticker cut, solid is a clean even line, offset throws a filled silhouette copy behind the subject (offset_x/offset_y place it), dotted walks dots along the edge. Pass style "none" to remove the stroke. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

style.description: Stroke style, or "none" to remove it

width.description: Ink thickness, design px at the 1080 short side, 1..60 (default 12)

feather.description: Edge softness: the ink blurred by this many design px, 0..40 (default 0, crisp)

offset_x.description: Offset style: silhouette displacement right, design px, -120..120

offset_y.description: Offset style: silhouette displacement down, design px, -120..120

tools.name: set_source_color
tools.title: Set source color
tools.description: Set what a source's code values mean — its color profile — for footage the header did not settle or the user wants read differently: rec709 (Rec.709: Display-referred video; no conversion); srgb (sRGB: Screen recordings and images; no conversion); apple-log (Apple Log: iPhone ProRes Log in the Rec.2020 gamut); apple-log-2 (Apple Log 2: iPhone Log in the Apple Wide Gamut); hlg (HLG: Rec.2100 hybrid log-gamma HDR video); pq (PQ: Rec.2100 PQ (HDR10) video). A log or HDR profile is converted to Rec.709 display values before any LUT or grade (Apple Log through the ACES output transform, HLG/PQ through BT.2100). "auto" returns the asset to the profile read from its file (editor_state.media shows each asset's sourceColor with what was detected). Pass assetId, or clipId for the clip's own source; every clip cut from that source changes with it. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

clipId.description: A video clip id — its source asset is the one changed

profile.description: Source profile, or "auto" for the detected one

tools.name: set_speed
tools.title: Set speed
tools.description: Set a video clip's playback speed, one rate across the whole clip, and/or play it backward. A still has no motion to retime and is refused; trim_clip is what changes how long it holds. Faster shortens the clip on the timeline; slower stretches it. Later clips, titles, captions, and soundtrack shift to stay in sync. A clip carrying a speed curve loses it when speed is passed: the rate becomes uniform again (set_speed_curve is the tool for a rate that changes through the footage). `reverse: true` plays the clip's trim backward, picture and sound, at its rate — the clip keeps its length and its curve, and its head now shows source `out`; `reverse: false` turns it forward again. `smooth: true` smooths the clip's slow motion: wherever its rate is under 1×, the frames between source frames are synthesized (the export estimates the motion between them) so the slow stretch moves without stepping; at 1× and above nothing changes. Turn it on for real slow motion from ordinary footage; `smooth: false` shows the source frames as they are. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

speed.description: Playback rate (1 = normal, no upper limit)

reverse.description: Play the footage backward (true) or forward (false)

smooth.description: Smooth slow motion: synthesize the frames between source frames wherever the rate is under 1×

tools.name: set_speed_curve
tools.title: Set speed curve
tools.description: Give a video clip (any track) a speed curve: its rate changes through the footage instead of being one number, so one clip can race through a walk, land on a beat, and hold on a face. A still is refused — it has no motion to retime. Nodes are {at, speed}: `at` in SOURCE seconds inside the clip's trim — the unit detect_beats, trim_clip and watch_video speak, so beat times drop straight in — and speed 0.1–10×. The rate curves smoothly between nodes and holds flat past the outermost ones; the whole list replaces the clip's curve, and an empty list clears it (the clip keeps its length at one uniform rate). Or pass a preset to lay a named ramp over the trim: flat (one rate across the clip); rampIn (opens fast and eases into slow motion); rampOut (opens in slow motion and eases out fast); drift (a rush that sinks into slow motion, then recovers); pulse (two rushes around a slow beat); hold (races in, slows into a moment in the middle, races out); whip (slow motion with a burst of speed in the middle); stutter (alternating rushes and slow beats). Technique: give a peak a beat of normal speed on either side or it reads as a glitch; below about 0.5× ordinary footage shows its own frame rate, so pass `smooth: true` with the curve — it synthesizes the frames between source frames wherever the rate is under 1× and leaves the faster stretches alone — unless the source is high-frame-rate already; sound stretches with its pitch kept, which holds up on speech to roughly 0.5–2×. The clip's timeline length becomes the integral of the curve and later items shift like a trim. Returns the resulting nodes, the clip's length before and after, and the rows that moved. In the UI the Speed Curve row opens the same graph over the timeline. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

nodes.description: The whole curve, any order; empty clears it

at.description: Source seconds, inside the clip's trim

preset.description: A named ramp laid over the clip's trim, instead of nodes

smooth.description: Smooth slow motion: synthesize the frames between source frames wherever the curve is under 1×

tools.name: set_split_edit
tools.title: Set split edit
tools.description: Split edit on a video clip: its sound starts ahead of its picture (lead — a J-cut, the next speaker heard before the cut) or carries on past it (tail — an L-cut, a voice running over the next shot). The extension plays the clip's own source from beyond its trim, under the neighbouring clip, ramping in from silence at the far end; pictures and clip positions stay where they are. Typical values: 0.05–0.5 s to soften a dialogue cut, 1–2 s to hand one scene into the next. Each side is capped at 5 s and at the source the clip has beyond its trim; 0 clears that side, and a side left out keeps its value. A cut carrying a transition keeps the transition's own handover, so that side plays no split edit. editor_state reports audioLead/audioTail on the clip. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

lead.description: Seconds the sound starts before the picture, 0..5 (0 clears)

tail.description: Seconds the sound carries past the picture's end, 0..5 (0 clears)

tools.name: set_track_hidden
tools.title: Set track hidden
tools.description: Hide or show a whole timeline row at once — the row's eye toggle. Applies to every item on that row: a hidden video track plays black and silent, a hidden soundtrack lane is silent, hidden text (title) lanes and subtitle tracks drop out of the picture, and hidden transitions leave their cuts hard. Items stay on the timeline, grayed. The transitions row is the only one of its kind, so omit `track` for it. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

tools.name: set_track_muted
tools.title: Set track muted
tools.description: Mute or unmute every clip on one video track at once — the track header's speaker toggle. The picture keeps playing. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

tools.name: set_transition
tools.title: Set transition
tools.description: Set the transition from this clip into the next clip on its track (any video track), in seconds (0 clears it, max 2). 0.5s suits a blend on the picture; the cross dissolve (audiocross) wants about 0.3s, since it is centered on the cut and both clips sound through it. A transition is a blend across the cut — it never moves, trims or overlaps clips, and it plays only while the pair touches. On upper tracks every style blends as an alpha dissolve (the tracks beneath show through). Only valid when a next same-track clip exists. Each edge holds one effect: setting a transition clears the animations adjacent to its joint (and set_animation on that edge replaces the transition). Read the transitions-and-fades skill before styling cuts. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

clipId.description: Video clip id (the clip the transition starts from)

ids.description: Several ids to change the same way, in place of clipId — one call, one undo step (select_items finds them)

seconds.description: Transition length in seconds, 0–2 (0 = hard cut)

feather.description: Softness of the reveal edge for wipeleft, wiperight, wipeup, wipedown, circleopen, circleclose, splitopen, splitclose: a share of the frame the edge crosses, 0..0.5 (0 = hard edge, 0.15 = a soft blurred band); other styles ignore it

band.description: A solid white panel running just ahead of the reveal edge of wipeleft, wiperight, wipeup, wipedown, as a share of the frame the edge crosses, 0..0.5 (0 = none): the outgoing shot is wiped first by white, then by the incoming one, and the panel leaves past the far edge. A 0.1s wiperight with band 0.5 is the white-panel slide of a recap montage. Draws a hard edge (overrides feather)

tools.name: set_transition_hidden
tools.title: Set transition hidden
tools.description: Hide or show one transition bar by its own id. A hidden bar stays on the transitions row (grayed) and keeps the cut it sits on, so nothing else claims that boundary, but plays nothing — the cut renders hard in the preview and in every export. Use it to try a cut without its blend; remove_transition is for deleting one outright. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

tools.name: split_at
tools.title: Split at
tools.description: Split items and their group members at a time, like pressing S: the items `ids` names, else the selection, else the video on track 0. Supported kinds: clip, audio, overlay, cue. Transitions remain whole. Omit t for the playhead. Times stay fixed; the result includes the new selected ids. It can move, overwrite or delete what the project already holds.

ids.description: Ids of the items to split, any track or kind (optional; default the selection)

tools.name: stock_add
tools.title: Stock add
tools.description: Import a stock video, image, or sound effect (by stock_search id) into the project. It previews as a card in this chat; pass add_to_timeline:true (or a `start`) to also drop it in the cut when the user asked — footage and stills on the video track, a sound on the soundtrack at the playhead (or `start`). Free — the media ships with Cut. It can move, overwrite or delete what the project already holds.

add_to_timeline.description: Place it in the cut — video track 0 for footage and stills, the soundtrack for a sound (default false — it stays on its chat card until the user asks)

start.description: Timeline start s (passing it implies add_to_timeline; default when placed: appended at the end)

tools.name: stock_search
tools.title: Stock search
tools.description: Search the bundled catalogs for footage, images, character references, and sound effects. Stock is free. Use stock_add to import a result, then inspect it before choosing where it belongs in the cut. Read-only: it changes nothing in the project or the account.

query.description: Words to match against prompts, categories, and tags (omit to browse)

tools.name: subtitles_add_track
tools.title: Subtitles add track
tools.description: Add a subtitle track for an additional language (up to 3, one language each — e.g. English on track 0, Korean on track 1; each shows as its own caption line, draggable to its own spot). The new track becomes active and starts empty: fill it with subtitles_translate_track, or subtitles_generate in its language. Plain "add captions" is subtitles_generate by itself — it writes the default track. It adds new items and leaves every existing one where it was.

language.description: The track's language as BCP-47, e.g. ko-KR (optional)

tools.name: subtitles_from_visuals
tools.title: Subtitles from visuals
tools.description: Caption a cut that has NO usable speech by watching sampled frames and writing timed narration captions (uses the user's Claude login to look at the frames). Use this instead of subtitles_generate when the video is silent b-roll, music-only, or otherwise has nothing to transcribe. Runs in the background; returns when finished. It can move, overwrite or delete what the project already holds.

locale.description: Caption language as BCP-47 like en-US (default: the track's language)

track.description: Subtitle track to write, 0-based (default: the active track)

tools.name: subtitles_generate
tools.title: Subtitles generate
tools.description: Transcribe the cut on-device (Apple speech) and create subtitle captions on a subtitle track (the active one unless `track` says otherwise; other tracks keep their captions) — it WRITES captions the user sees, so call it only when they asked for subtitles; to just hear what an audio asset says, listen_audio. Cue times come back snapped to the audio, so treat them as in sync — retime a cue only when the user points at one. Runs in the background; returns when finished. If no speech is found, no subtitles are added. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

locale.description: Speech language as BCP-47 like en-US (default: the track's language)

track.description: Subtitle track to write, 0-based (default: the active track)

tools.name: subtitles_remove_track
tools.title: Subtitles remove track
tools.description: Remove a subtitle track and its captions; higher tracks shift down. Removing the only track empties it — so this also answers "delete the subtitles". It can move, overwrite or delete what the project already holds.

tools.name: subtitles_set_view
tools.title: Subtitles set view
tools.description: Toggle subtitles on the video (preview + export burn-in) and/or the timeline cue track. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

tools.name: subtitles_translate_track
tools.title: Subtitles translate track
tools.description: Translate existing captions into another language on their own subtitle track — the way to answer "add Korean subtitles". Reuses the track already set to that language or adds one (max 3), then translates the source track's cues one-to-one, timings kept. The captions must exist first (subtitles_generate). It can move, overwrite or delete what the project already holds.

language.description: Target language as BCP-47, e.g. ko-KR

from_track.description: Source track, 0-based (default: the first track with captions)

tools.name: suggest_font
tools.title: Suggest font
tools.description: Name the face a reference's type is set in: reads the source's frame at t, lifts the ink inside region off its ground, and ranks every face Donkey can set a title in — each bundled family at each bundled weight, the system set and the account's own fonts — by how closely its glyphs for the same words match, tracking solved so each runs as wide as the reference. Call it for each distinct face while rebuilding a reference's titles, so the font, weight, size and tracking come from the frame. Pass the words exactly as they read, case and line breaks included, and a region close around them read off watch_video at detail original. Returns the best faces with score (0..1), size (px at the 1080 short side, for the same ink height) and tracking (em), and x/y, where that face's title sits (add_title's x/y) for its ink to land on the reference's — a title is set from the middle of its line, so its ink centre is off it. `ink` is the ink's own box, centre and size in frame fractions. Cards in one face share its weight, size and tracking, but each sits its own way in its space, so read each card for its own x/y rather than setting the rest from the first one's place. Type set at an angle — a column word reading bottom to top — is read upright: pass `rotation`, the angle add_title would set it at (-90 reads bottom to top, 90 top to bottom), with a region around the word as it stands; one line of words in a region taller than wide is tried both ways round without it, and `rotation` comes back with the result to set on the title. verdict no_match means nothing bundled is close: the reference uses a face Donkey does not bundle, so say so and name the stand-in you use, of its kind — `kinds` lists every face by kind (serif, sans, script, display, mono), each as its id and a few words on its look. Whatever face you set — a stand-in, or one you picked over the top match by eye — call again with `fonts: [its id]` for its own size, tracking and x/y on this ink; never guess a size. `inkPx` is how tall a line of the ink runs in the source; under 24 the result is `small`: the glyphs have blurred into their proportions, the ranking cannot tell a serif from a condensed sans, so name the face by eye at detail original and take the closest of its kind from `kinds`. Read-only: it changes nothing in the project or the account.

asset_id.description: Project asset id of the reference (video or image)

t.description: Source second the type shows at (default 0)

x.description: Centre x, frame fraction

y.description: Centre y, frame fraction

text.description: The words the region shows, as they read, with a line break where the type breaks

rotation.description: Degrees the type is turned, as add_title's rotation: -90 reads bottom to top, 90 top to bottom (default: upright, or both ways for one line in a tall region)

fonts.description: Font ids to score instead of every face — the stand-in you picked, so its size, tracking and x/y come from the frame

x.description: Centre x, fraction of the whole frame's width

y.description: Centre y, fraction of the whole frame's height

w.description: Width, fraction of the whole frame's width

h.description: Height, fraction of the whole frame's height

picture.description: Read inside this box of the source's frame, or "full" for the whole frame. Default: the picture box find_picture keeps on the source, else the whole frame. Every x, y, w, h the call takes and returns is a fraction of it.

tools.name: switch_timeline
tools.title: Switch timeline
tools.description: Open another of the project's 3 timelines (main = Main, second = Second, third = Third) — the picker at the left of the timeline toolbar. Each timeline holds its own clips, soundtrack, transitions, elements, subtitles and aspect ratio; the media and the project settings are shared. The preview, the export and every other tool work on the open one, which editor_state project.timeline names, with project.timelines summarizing each. A timeline opened for the first time is empty at Main's aspect ratio, and each keeps its own undo history. A share link plays the timeline its share settings pick, Main by default. There are exactly these 3; none can be added, renamed or deleted. It changes only the editor's view of the project.

tools.name: sync_audio
tools.title: Sync audio
tools.description: Dual-system sound: line up a separately recorded audio file (a lavalier, a recorder, a second camera's mic) with a video by matching it against the camera's own sound, then bind it to the video. Every clip of that video — the ones on the timeline now and any split, trimmed, sped, reversed, or copied later — plays the recording through its own trim and speed, and the camera's track goes quiet; the preview, every export, captions, and the listening tools all hear the recording. Name the video by clipId (one of its clips) or assetId, and the recording by audio_asset_id (an audio file in the project). The match reports `offset` (recording seconds = video seconds + offset) and `confidence`; when no single alignment stands out — a different take, or two files with no sound in common — it refuses and binds nothing, and the user can pick another file. clear: true returns the video to its own sound. editor_state shows each bound video's `soundFrom` on its media entry. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

clipId.description: A video clip whose source video gets the recording

assetId.description: The video asset to bind, when no clip names it

audio_asset_id.description: The audio asset holding the clean recording

clear.description: Unbind the recording: the video plays its own sound again

tools.name: sync_lyrics
tools.title: Sync lyrics
tools.description: Time a text the user already has — song lyrics, a script, a poem — to the audio in the cut, and put it on a caption track. Transcribes the cut first when the track is empty, then aligns the user's words to the recognized ones and keeps the user's text exactly as written: the recognizer supplies the clock, never the wording, which is what makes it work on singing it half-mishears. Words it missed take interpolated times from the words around them. Pass `look` to dress the track in a text-videos look at the same time (karaoke word highlight included) — only when the user asked for a designed run; without it the captions keep the track's current styling. For lyrics as full-frame cards rather than captions, follow this with add_text_sequence from_captions. It overwrites an existing value; the same call again gives the same result.

text.description: The lyrics or script, one line per screen (newline separated)

track.description: Subtitle track to write, 0-based (default: the active track)

look.description: Text-videos look id to dress the captions in

from.description: Ignore audio before this timeline second

to.description: Ignore audio after this timeline second

background.description: With `look`, also set the project background to its frame color (default: whatever the look does — the designed looks paint it, plain and over-footage leave it alone)

tools.name: template_add
tools.title: Template add
tools.description: Re-materialize a snippet into the project: its clips, overlays, titles, and captions land editable, exactly as saved (clip layers append to track 0; free-positioned parts line up at the playhead). A Library snippet's media import as assets on the way in; a snippet saved in this project's own Media reuses the media already here. Call it only when the user asked for the snippet in the cut. It adds new items and leaves every existing one where it was.

id.description: Snippet id — from library_list, or the id carried by a snippet the user referenced

tools.name: template_gallery
tools.title: Template gallery
tools.description: List Donkey's template gallery — ready-made edits every account can start from, each with sample footage in its clips, styled titles and effects, and often a soundtrack timed to its cuts. Each entry gives its id, name, what it is for, frame shape, length, how many footage slots and texts it has, whether it carries music, and its link. Filter by category, aspect, length or style, and pass `query` to find templates from a description in the user's own words, best fit first; all are optional. Results come a page at a time with the total; `next` is the offset of the following page. Read-only: it changes nothing in the project or the account.

query.description: What the user is looking for, described in their words (up to 300 characters): subject, purpose, mood, look

length.description: short ≤15 s, medium ≤30 s, long beyond

offset.description: Where the page starts; pass the previous page's next

tools.name: template_use
tools.title: Template use

tools.name: track_camera
tools.title: Track camera
tools.description: Measure how the camera moves over a stretch of a video, inside its picture: each frame's zoom, shift and turn against the frame on `from`, so a punch-in, a push, a beat zoom pulse or a shake is keyed with set_clip_keyframes to the reference's own numbers. Give one shot's stretch (SOURCE seconds; a cut inside it breaks the read). `path` lists every frame: t, scale (1.08 is 8% closer), dx/dy (how far the picture's centre moved, fractions of the frame, + is right and down), rotation (degrees clockwise) and residual (what the move leaves unexplained, 0..255 a pixel; null on a frame too blurred to read). A frame whose picture moves in two layers — a cutout held still over a background that shakes, or pulsing over a still one — also has `second`, the other layer's pose and the `share` of the picture it holds: build it as two tracks, the footage keyed with one pose and its cutout (set_removal) above it keyed with the other. The keys copy it straight across: a clip key at the same moment with scale, rotation, and x = 0.5 + dx, y = 0.5 + dy — relative to the first frame, so start the clip's own pose there. `moves` lists each move of each number with from/to, start/end, the ease that fits it (linear, sine.in, sine.out, sine.inOut, power2.in, power2.out, power2.inOut, power3.in, power3.out, power3.inOut) and `error`; a pulse is a move out and a move back. A zoom about a point off the centre — the picture growing away from one spot — adds `anchor`, that frame point (frame fractions): a zoom through a title's letter is a dive exit with out_anchor there. `still` true means one picture holds under the whole move — residual under 6 throughout: the reference froze that frame and moved it, so freeze_frame the shot's clip at `from` and key the moves on the freeze. A live shot with a moving camera leaves a higher residual: its numbers are still the move. Up to 120 frames a call; when `truncated`, continue from `coveredTo`. Read-only: it changes nothing in the project or the account.

tools.name: track_element
tools.title: Track element
tools.description: Measure where an element of a source's picture sits, frame by frame, and how it moves, so a grow, a slide or a pop is keyed with set_overlay_keyframes to the reference's own numbers. Give a stretch of a video (SOURCE seconds) and a `seed` box on the element at `from`; boxes in and out are x/y centre and w/h size as frame fractions — what add_shape, add_title and the keys take. The element is found by colour: `color` (sample_color reads it), or else the seed's median colour on the first frame, so draw the seed inside the element's edges at a moment it is on screen. `match` shape follows the one connected piece of that colour the seed sits on — a card, a bar, a sticker — as it moves and changes size; ink takes every pixel of that colour inside the seed (or `within`), the ink of a line of type whose letters are separate pieces: its centre is where the title sits and its height is about 0.7 of the font size when the line is capitals. letters reads a line of type coming in letter by letter — a drop, a rise, a fall out of focus, digits rolling in on a slot reel, letters popping in where they stand: give `text` (the words as they read), `to` a moment just after the last letter lands, `from` before the first one shows, and a seed close around the landed line; it returns each letter's timing (shows, starts, lands, alpha, soft — the defocus it shows in at) and `entrance`, the whole entrance as set_overlay_animation takes it — a reel comes back as in_style slot with its turn, spacing, band and landing bounce, letters that appear without moving as a typewriter — plus `crosses`, other ink the letters pass in front of or behind, which says which lane goes in front. Leave out `to` to measure one frame. `moves` lists each move of x, y, w and h with from/to (the source seconds it starts and lands), start/end values, the ease that fits it (linear, sine.in, sine.out, sine.inOut, power2.in, power2.out, power2.inOut, power3.in, power3.out, power3.inOut) and `error`, the RMS miss as a share of the move: under 0.03 is that curve, over 0.1 none fits and the move keys from `path` point by point. A size move keys as scale: w over the element's resting w. `path` lists the box wherever it changes (a hold is one entry); a null box is a frame where the element was not found. Up to 360 frames a call; when `truncated`, continue from `coveredTo`. Works on a still image too (one frame). Read-only: it changes nothing in the project or the account.
